scope.target: Approved Project views, allowlisted workflows, final provider readback, repository validation, and PR-only closeout.
constraints: Configure only Active Backlog, Roadmap, Owner Review, and History by Release views.
Configure only issue-opened auto-add with Status Inbox and issue-closed Status Done outcomes.
Do not enable PR-merge closure or any provider-to-repository reverse write.
Record unsupported provider capabilities explicitly and do not invent completion.

steps: Configure and read back approved Project views.
Inspect existing workflows and configure only the two allowlisted outcomes.
Run complete provider and repository validation.
Close workflow evidence and publish through the PR-only main policy.
validation: View names/layouts/filters/grouping/sorts and enabled workflow outcomes match the approved provider contract or carry explicit provider-constraint evidence.
All Issue, Project, receipt, test, workflow, and Git handoff evidence passes without making GitHub a repository workflow dependency.
execution.last_completed_step: Exactly read back four saved views and three enabled provider workflows implementing the two allowlisted outcomes.
execution.next_action: Publish the completed workflow through the repository's PR-only main integration policy.

results.summary: Configured and read back Active Backlog, Roadmap, Owner Review, and History by Release; retained only the auto-add/Inbox and closed/Done automation outcomes; disabled template PR and lifecycle side effects outside the allowlist.
tests_run: GraphQL ProjectV2View readback: four exact names, layouts, filters, groups, and sorts
Signed-in Project workflow UI readback: three enabled workflows, five-item open auto-add query, Status Inbox initialization, and Status Done closure
Signed-in Active Backlog readback: four named views, 5 matching open items, and Workflows (3 enabled)
results.residual_risk: The built-in auto-add trigger also evaluates updated Issues that newly match is:issue is:open; this is the provider-native implementation of the approved issue-opened outcome. History ordering uses Title ascending because titles begin with the canonical backlog ID and no redundant Backlog ID field was approved.
